subject.title: RFC: Distributed Agent Runtime — separate control plane from agent compute

question: Should OpenClaw pursue the Gateway control-plane and per-agent runtime split as a core architecture track, and what first milestone should be supported?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the first implementation would set public protocol, config, lifecycle, security, migration, and deployment boundaries that require maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve Phased Runtime Split
options.body: Keep this issue canonical and sponsor a first local-split milestone that defines runtime registration, trust, session ownership, channel delivery, and per-agent lifecycle before remote/container backends.

options.title: Narrow To Execution Placement
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/82017 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/84758 as the current scope while deferring the broader Gateway/runtime split.

options.title: Defer Core Architecture Change
options.body: Continue supporting separate-gateway/operator workarounds and decline first-class distributed runtime support until stronger maintainer demand or design proof appears.

recommendation.title: Approve Phased Runtime Split
recommendation.body: Keep this issue canonical and sponsor a first local-split milestone that defines runtime registration, trust, session ownership, channel delivery, and per-agent lifecycle before remote/container backends.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest concrete history on the worker-runtime isolation experiment and is the best available owner for the architecture direction choice.
